scope: Seven identified historical independent decision files in the retained October directory; not a complete review of the chapter or all historical artifacts. Historical repair IDs are local to their source generation and may collide with current IDs. Do not reuse IDs, manufacture missing citations, or migrate approvals by changing hashes.

historicalFieldReplacements.before: In Long'an 4 (AD 400), he claimed the imperial title at the southern suburban altar, issued a general amnesty, inaugurated the Jianping era, established a traveling ancestral temple south of the palace, and sent envoys bearing the accession proclamation.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: In Long'an 4 (AD 400), at the southern suburb he assumed the imperial throne—an act the history presents as usurpation—issued a general amnesty, adopted the Jianping era name, established a temporary ancestral temple south of the palace, and sent envoys with a document to report the accomplishment there.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: Restore the reporting act in 告成 without specifying the document, recipient, or accomplishment more narrowly than the source. Temporary ancestral temple is a contextual rendering of 行廟. The retained Long’an 4 / AD 400 contextual date needs independent date review.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 四年，僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦，改元為建平，設行廟于宮南，遣使奉策告成焉。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: In Long'an 4 (AD 400), he claimed the imperial title at the southern suburban altar, issued a general amnesty, inaugurated the Jianping era, established a traveling ancestral temple south of the palace, and sent envoys bearing the accession proclamation.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: Revise to restore the locative 焉, read as the immediately preceding temporary temple; this antecedent is plausible but interpretative. Attribute the evaluative 僭 to the history, not objective fact. Keep the document and reported accomplishment unspecified. The AD conversion in the idiomatic field remains unaudited.

historicalFieldReplacements.before: He opened ironworks on Mount Shang and salt monopolies at Wuchang Marsh to swell the army's coffers.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: He established smelting works on Mount Shang and a salt office at Wuchang Marsh to increase resources for the army and the state.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: The source specifies smelting and a salt administration for military and state use, but not iron, monopolies, or army coffers.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 立冶于商山，置鹽官于烏常澤，以廣軍國之用。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: He opened ironworks on Mount Shang and salt monopolies at Wuchang Marsh to swell the army's coffers.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 冶 is smelting, not specifically iron; 鹽官 is a salt administration rather than necessarily monopolies; 軍國 includes both military and state. Source: 立冶于商山，置鹽官于烏常澤，以廣軍國之用。
冶 does not specify iron, 鹽官 is a salt office, and 軍國 includes military and state use; the existing idiom adds unsupported details.

originalWitness.excerpt: 立冶于商山，置鹽官于烏常澤，以廣軍國之用。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Duan Hong and the rest heard the alarm and sealed the four gates with troops.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: Duan Hong and the others heard of the palace disturbance and stationed their troops at the four gates.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: The source places troops at the four gates but does not say they were sealed. 勒兵 also suggests mustering or commanding troops; this narrow correction does not resolve that nuance.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: The palace disturbance prompts Duan Hong and others to deploy troops at the four gates; the Chinese does not explicitly say the gates were sealed. This narrow proposal leaves the muster or command nuance of 勒兵 implicit.

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Murong De re-entered the palace, executed Hou Chimei's faction, and Murong Da fled to Wei.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: Murong De entered the palace and executed Hou Chimei and the others; Murong Da fled in fear to Wei.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: 赤眉等 means Chimei and others, not necessarily a faction; 達懼 expressly gives Da’s fear. Names follow the immediately preceding context.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 德入宮，誅赤眉等，達懼而奔魏。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: Murong De re-entered the palace, executed Hou Chimei's faction, and Murong Da fled to Wei.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: De enters the palace and executes Chimei and others; Da flees to Wei in fear. The expanded names Hou Chimei and Murong Da are given in the preceding context, s0212.

originalWitness.excerpt: 德入宮，誅赤眉等，達懼而奔魏。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou closed Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou raised a mound over Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: In 武王封比干之墓, the transmitted gloss 積土為封 explains heaping earth over the tomb; “closed” wrongly suggests sealing the tomb rather than the commemorative mound action.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 邃答曰：「武王封比干之墓，漢祖祭信陵之墳，皆留心賢哲，每懷往事。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: Sui replied, 'King Wu of Zhou closed Bi Gan's tomb, Han's Gaozu sacrificed at Lord Xinling's grave—both fixed their hearts on worthies and often cherished old deeds.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: The Jin shu states that King Wu acted on Bi Gan's tomb; the parallel Shiji Music Treatise preserves Zheng Xuan's gloss that this was heaping earth. The revised wording expresses that sense without adding a date or physical details.

originalWitness.citation: Shiji Music Treatise, Zheng Xuan gloss, https://www.xuoda.com/ls/shiji2/102.htm

In 仇齊 Qi is the object of Xi Ke’s hostility, as 楚 is the object of Zixu’s resentment, not the party he avenged.

originalWitness.excerpt: 德登高望之，顧謂劉軌、高雅之曰：「昔郤克仇齊，子胥怨楚，終能暢其剛烈，名流千載。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Murong Chao, whom he had summoned from Chang'an, now arrived.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: De's nephew Murong Chao, whom De had earlier sought to bring from Chang'an, now arrived.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: Restore 兄子, his elder brother’s son, without claiming a named father. The related literal translation needs separate review of 迎.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: Murong Chao, his elder brother's son, whom he had summoned from Chang'an, now arrived.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 兄子 explicitly establishes De’s elder brother’s son. 迎 can mean go to meet or fetch; summoned is too definite, so use sought to bring without deciding who traveled. Source: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
兄子 identifies Chao as De’s elder brother’s son. 迎 does not by itself establish the precise means, so the narrower reviewed wording avoids asserting a summons.

originalWitness.excerpt: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Earlier, De had welcomed his brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point he arrived.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: Earlier, De had sought to bring his brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point Chao arrived.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: The later arrival should not become an earlier completed welcome. This pairs with the previously reviewed idiomatic wording without asserting a precise means of 迎.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: Earlier, De had summoned his elder brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point he arrived.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: The earlier 迎 action precedes Chao's arrival. 'Sought to bring' is interpretive: 迎 may mean to go meet or fetch, and the precise method and any unsuccessful attempt are not established.

originalWitness.excerpt: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: He named Murong Chao crown prince and issued a broad amnesty.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince and granting a general amnesty throughout the realm; sons succeeding their fathers were each granted two grades of rank.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: Restore the rank-grant provision 子為父後者人爵二級. Its exact scope and phrasing require an independent editorial decision.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty within his realm, and raised by two degrees the rank of every son who was his father’s heir.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 子為父後者 identifies sons succeeding fathers, and 人爵二級 grants each two grades of rank. Increase could suggest everyone already held rank, which the text does not say. Source: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
子為父後者人爵二級 grants two grades to sons succeeding their fathers; an increase would imply an existing rank that the wording does not require.

originalWitness.excerpt: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince, amnestied the realm, and for sons continuing fathers raised each man's rank two grades.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince and granting an amnesty throughout the realm; sons succeeding their fathers were each granted two grades of rank.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: The rank grant does not require a prior rank; match the independently revised idiomatic field without asserting an increase.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince, amnestied the realm, and for sons continuing fathers raised each man's rank two grades.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: The text grants qualifying sons two grades of rank without explicitly asserting that each previously held a rank; this aligns the literal with the reviewed idiomatic field.

originalWitness.excerpt: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: That night they prepared more than ten coffins and sent them out through the four gates, burying him secretly in the mountain valleys; in the end, no one knew where his body lay.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: 棺 means coffins, not coffers; preserve the number, nocturnal setting and uncertain location. The text does not explicitly identify any particular coffin as a decoy.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 乃夜為十餘棺，分出四門，潛葬山谷，竟不知其屍之所在。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: They ran decoy coffers out each gate and hid his true burial in the hills.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 十餘棺 specifies over ten coffins; 夜, 分出四門, 潛葬山谷 and 竟不知其屍之所在 provide the night, four gates, concealed burial and unknown resting place. The suggested wording restores these details without inventing an identified decoy coffin.

originalWitness.excerpt: 乃夜為十餘棺，分出四門，潛葬山谷，竟不知其屍之所在。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: His temple posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: His posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu, a title this history treats as illegitimate.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: 諡 is a posthumous title, not a temple name; 偽 expresses the historiographer’s delegitimizing judgment. Independently review its appropriate English rendering.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 偽諡獻武皇帝。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: His temple posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 諡 is the posthumous designation, not a temple name. 偽 expresses this history's claim of illegitimacy; the proposed 'Jin historian' risks misidentifying the compiler's period. Zizhi Tongjian 114 separately distinguishes 諡獻武皇帝 from 廟號世宗.

originalWitness.citation: Jinshu 127, s0279, sealed dossier; compare Zizhi Tongjian 114
originalWitness.excerpt: 偽諡獻武皇帝。

historicalFieldReplacements.before: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.
historicalFieldReplacements.after: His posthumous title was Emperor Xianwu, a title this history treats as illegitimate.
historicalFieldReplacements.sourceReason: 偽諡 marks a posthumous title as illegitimate from the historiographer’s perspective; this formulation needs independent contextual and stylistic review.
historicalFieldReplacements.currentChinese: 偽諡獻武皇帝。
historicalFieldReplacements.currentText: He was posthumously titled Emperor Xianwu.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 偽 expresses the source's judgment of illegitimacy, while 諡 is a posthumous title. Avoid 'the Jin historian': the Book of Jin is a later compilation, so that label misleadingly suggests an author from the Jin period. The wording attributes the judgment to this history rather than endorsing it.

originalWitness.excerpt: 偽諡獻武皇帝。
